Nothing was committed, stashed, checked out or reset; the worktree stays uncommitted as instructed, and I read the root checkout / Codex source read-only and touched no other worktree or Docker. I started `next dev -p 3007` from this worktree for the measurements and stopped it afterwards (PID 45104, `Stop-Process -Id 45104 -Force` -> "stopped"; port 3007 is free for the driver).

Three things for the lead:

1. S2's blast radius is bigger AND smaller than the ruling assumed. The rule spans THIRTEEN selectors, not eight (marketing.css 6236-6249: `.cta-block p:not(.eyebrow)`, `.cta-block > div > span`, `.cta-block .eyebrow`, `.eyebrow`, `.record-caption`, `.card-eyebrow`, `.tour-example-label`, `.form-kicker`, `.photo-credit`, `.retailer-art figcaption`, `.story-section figcaption`, `.scene-fallback > p`, `.footer-app-note`) — but a later `!important` overrides it for all but four grounds, so the value change only moves `.card-eyebrow` (/pricing), `.photo-credit` (/company), `.retailer-art figcaption` (/retailers) and `.tour-example-label` (/wholesalers, /distributors). Notably it does NOT reach the dark `.cta-block` (#10264d) or the dark `.eyebrow` section (#292c33), where a darker value would have been a regression — those keep their own #d8dbe1 / #ffd09a at 10.5-10.8:1. Worth pinning in the close-out so a future round does not "simplify" the cascade and hand this rule the dark grounds.

2. Dead selectors for the css-consolidation close-out row: `.story-section figcaption`, `.scene-fallback > p` and `.footer-app-note` render on no marketing route at either viewport (`.story-section`, `.scene-fallback` and `.footer-app-note` appear in no ported `.tsx` — the only mention is the `.story-section` string inside `components/editorial-motion.tsx:12`), yet they carry CSS at marketing.css 1469-1503 / 4782-4826 / 1628 / 4978-4988 / 5916-5933 / 8762 and elsewhere. Either the port dropped the markup that used them or the source ships them dead too — worth one grep at consolidation time.

3. S3 is a real source defect, not a port defect: the Codex source has the same `#ffffffb5` panel and `#6d8dad` eyebrow (glass.css 828-845 region / the `.company-image > div > span` rule), so the port now deviates from the source by two values. That deviation is documented inline at marketing.css 5364-5371 and 5380-5385 in the same style as the round-5 contrast comments, but it belongs on the S5 "carried to the owner" list as a deliberate accessibility deviation from the redesign.

Not done (out of my scope by the design): the UI driver/judge flows, the ownerReviewPack selection, the S4 registry row, and `npm run lint -w apps/web` + `node scripts/validate-lessons.mjs` (the Final Haiku gate).

ownerNotes: The site is quieter and greyer than the design you signed off on. The new stylesheet is assembled from the redesign's own files in the redesign's own order, and the last layer in that stack is a grey-toned pass that overrides colours and type sizes set earlier — it repaints the page background plain white, pushes body text to a near-black grey, and shrinks a number of small labels. The result reads clean and calm, but several coloured surfaces the written design brief describes come out flatter and more neutral on the live page than in the brief's prose. Nothing is broken; this is a look-and-feel call. Decide whether you want the coloured chrome restored to match the brief, or the calmer grey treatment kept as the real design.

Every big headline's second line is styled as emphasis in the markup but renders upright, not slanted — 'Let's get you / back on track.', 'A plan that fits / your working day.', 'Orders. Deliveries. Accounts. / Finally, connected.' The second line does get its own colour (navy, teal or green depending on the page), so the two-tone effect is there, but there is no italic. If you expected an italic second line, that is a deliberate change worth confirming before launch.

The contact and demo forms do not send anything to us. Filling one in opens the visitor's own email program with a pre-written draft addressed to hello@routeflow.info; the visitor still has to press send, and if their device has no mail app set up, nothing happens beyond a fallback line showing the address. There is no server behind the form, so nothing is stored, nothing is tracked, and no lead is captured if the visitor abandons the draft. If marketing needs a real enquiry pipeline, that is a separate piece of work to commission.

Two text colours now differ from the redesign on purpose, for legibility. Small captions and labels across the site were a shade too light to meet the accessibility contrast standard on their tinted backgrounds, and the caption text sitting on the frosted card over the warehouse photograph on the About page was far below it — that card was translucent enough that the text's readability changed with whatever part of the photo happened to sit behind it. The captions were darkened one step, and the frosted card was made more opaque so the text reads the same regardless of the photo. Both are small, both keep the original colour family, and both are deviations from what the designers shipped. Confirm you are happy carrying them, or ask for the designers' own fix instead.

The custom 'page not found' screen only appears on desktop. On phones, any address we do not recognise is handed to the mobile app instead, and the app decides what to show — so a visitor who mistypes a URL on a phone will not see the branded error page in the review pack. Fixing this properly means keeping a maintained list of which addresses belong to the app, which is a real piece of work. Decide whether that is worth doing now or noted and deferred.

The marketing pages are light-mode only. The redesign shipped a dark colour scheme, and it was deliberately left out of this port, so these pages will always render light even for a visitor whose device is set to dark. If you want dark mode on the public site, it is an add-on to schedule rather than something that was lost.

- My own pngjs harness (scratchpad/rev7/m.mjs): region stats (distinct-colour count, modal + share, darkest/lightest by luminance, mean), an exact-colour locator with bbox and row histogram, a row profiler, and a WCAG contrast calculator. Every ratio in my verdicts is from that calculator, not copied.
- Gates in .../rf-watchdog/apps/web: prettier --check exit 0, tsc --noEmit exit 0, jest --silent 42 suites / 338 tests passed exit 0.

WHERE I ADDED SOMETHING THE DRIVER AND JUDGE DID NOT HAVE:
1. I located the /retailers figure independently by scanning for its own background colour (#def5ee bbox x19-355, y668-1058) instead of trusting the reported box — so the 15,213-colour count is anchored to geometry I derived, and S1's refutation no longer rests on anyone else's crop.
2. I traced the full `!important` cascade selector by selector. That is what actually answers "any side effect on the eight selectors" — and the answer is better than assumed: the rule spans thirteen selectors, nine are overridden downstream, and the two DARK grounds (`.cta-block` on #10264d, `.difference-section` on --charcoal) are provably unreachable by the darker value. A darker value landing on those would have been a real regression; it cannot.
3. I verified the alpha arithmetic behind S3's floor (0xdb/255 = 0.8588 → #dbdbdb) rather than accepting the stated floor, and confirmed why blur cannot break it. That is what makes S3 sound at viewports nobody captured post-fix.
4. I row-profiled the /company panel myself and found the same right edge (~x495) the judge found, which independently confirms both the contamination in W7's first sample and the correctness of the inset numbers.
5. I found one thing neither the driver, the judge, nor W7 reported: the rule at marketing.css:6237, immediately above the one S2 fixed, paints #5e718c body copy on the #e4f6ef `.retailer-start`/`.retailer-price` panel at 4.441:1 — 382 px of that exact ink inside the panel on desktop and 383 on mobile, pixel-proven, with the ground confirmed from a clean strip. That is a genuine AA failure on shipping text.

WHY I STILL RULE LAND. All three of the round's rulings are discharged on evidence I reproduced myself: S1 is by-design on re-verified source lines plus a 380×-over-threshold pixel proof, S2 and S3 are fixed with every ground measured and every ratio re-derived, the gates are green, and there is no regression anywhere in the cascade. The new #5e718c hazard is real but it is pre-existing, faithful to the Codex source (glass.css:1872), 0.06 short of the threshold, and outside every ruling the lead wrote for this round — reopening on it would be re-scoping mid-flight rather than finishing. It belongs in the same lane as the other deliberate deviations: the S5 owner list and the CSS-consolidation close-out row, where the owner is already being asked to accept two darkened text colours. If the lead wants the marketing port to ship AA-clean on body copy — a defensible call, and the only reason I would flip to one-more-round — this is a single-declaration round 8 of exactly the shape S2 already proved, and #5c6f8a clears every ground I measured. I have given the value and the numbers so that decision costs the lead nothing to make.

Two smaller gaps I would put in the close-out rather than in a new round: /pricing and /company-mobile were never captured post-fix, and I closed both by construction (cascade + pinned grounds for /pricing; the photo-independent floor for /company mobile) rather than by pixels of the new colour on those surfaces.
